rule: Stated before any paid router call (committed with this file). Backlog: synth_dev (60), synth_clean_dev (first 30) and CODEBRIM dev100, 190 photos in a seeded shuffle; per-photo engine v1 (onnx:drishyam_dacl10k.onnx, its FP16 net as the fast model) on the fixed costs of results/local-macos-x86-dacl10k-retime/micro.json, default per-photo caps, governor on. Router: Nova Lite (amazon.nova-lite-v1:0, us-east-1, temperature 0) with the fixed prompt of drishyam/router.py, one call per photo, cached. Primary metric: critical recall within budget, the share of the backlog's labelled critical defects that a critical finding queues for a person before the batch budget runs out, at a total budget of half the seconds the 190 jobs take run in full. The rule-triage arm and the router arm are charged their triage seconds, and the router arm also its Bedrock $ as seconds at the agent's $0.339 per hour. Gain: the paired 95 % bootstrap CI (1000 resamples of the photos within each of the three splits) of router / rule triage lies above 1, and so does that of router / random order (mean of 1000 seeded permutations; 100 per resample). Harm: either CI lies below 1. Otherwise: no measurable difference. Safety, reported with the verdict: the router's miss rate, the share of photos holding a labelled critical defect that it clears, with a Wilson 95 % CI; clearing is called safe only if that CI's upper bound is at most 0.05. Reported, not part of the verdict: the other budgets (a quarter, three quarters), the router arm with its $ not charged, IoU-only recall, time to the first queued critical defect, label agreement with the labels (Critical: a labelled critical defect; Requires zoom: any other labelled defect; Clear: no labelled defect), cost, latency and fallbacks by cause.
